description: The reserved automatic events (SPEC.md → Automatic events) and their conformance flows. `commonProperties` and `reserved` are the machine-readable catalogue: SDKs, the server, and the PR agent read the names from here. Each case runs on a harness that controls what the platform reports (`device`, and the app version and build on each `launch`), the lifecycle signals, and the SDK clock. A case starts on the storage named by `storage` (default `empty`); storage survives `terminate`. The values the harness cannot control are placeholders: `$platform` (bound to the SDK's own `platform`, and `os_name` carries the same value), `$sdk_name`, and `$sdk_version`; the harness substitutes its SDK's values and checks them against `commonProperties`. `launch` starts the process: the harness builds the client with the case `config` (automatic events on unless `config.automaticEvents` is false), calls identify('user_1') right after it, and then delivers the first foreground (a cold start). `background` and `foreground` move the harness clock forward by `afterMs` and then deliver that signal. `terminate` ends the process with no further signal. `screen` calls the SDK's manual screen API. `pushOpened` hands the notification data payload to the SDK's push-open API. `pushPermission` reports this notification permission through the SDK's permission API; an SDK whose API names the statuses differently maps them (granted is authorized, undetermined is not_determined). The harness makes the platform permission unreadable, so only `pushPermission` steps report it. `reset` calls reset(). `optOut` and `optIn` call the SDK's opt-out and opt-in APIs. The harness flushes after every step, then collects every event the case sent on /v1/events/batch and /v1/events/track, in send order, and asserts that they equal `expectedEvents`: the same `event_type` and exactly the same `properties`, after it removes identity fields, `occurred_at`, and `context` (context must still carry `$message_id`, as wire.json pins). Identify requests are not compared. An SDK whose lifecycle clock the harness cannot set checks instead that `foreground_ms` is a non-negative integer. SDKs that also implement automatic screen capture run these cases with it off. Every OTHER conformance harness (wire.json, behavior.json, push.json, anonymous.json, v2.json) runs the SDK with automatic events disabled, so those fixtures see only the requests their steps cause. Contract v2 push events are in `pushEventsV2` (opt-in, with its own supersedes list).

app_version.description: The user-facing app version (CFBundleShortVersionString, versionName, package version).

app_build.description: The build number as a string (CFBundleVersion, versionCode).

platform.description: The OS family, never the framework name: an iPad is ios, a React Native app on Android is android, a Flutter desktop app is macos, windows or linux. Readers treat any other value as other; the server never rejects an event for it.

os_name.description: The same lowercase OS family value as platform.

os_version.description: The operating system version as the platform reports it, for example 18.2 or 15.

sdk_name.description: The SDK that sent the event.

sdk_version.description: The SDK release version, for example 1.8.0.

locale.description: BCP 47 language tag of the device, for example de-DE.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name of the device, for example Europe/Berlin. Never an abbreviation or an offset.

timezone_offset_minutes.description: Minutes east of UTC at send time, for example 120. Sent only when the IANA name is unknown; never together with timezone.

reserved.name: app_installed
reserved.trigger: First launch of an install: no stored app version and no earlier SDK state.

reserved.name: app_updated
reserved.trigger: A launch where the app version or build differs from the stored one.

previous_version.description: The stored app version before this launch.

previous_build.description: The stored build before this launch.

reserved.name: app_opened
reserved.trigger: Every move to the foreground, including the cold start.

cold_start.description: true for the first foreground of the process, false for a return from the background. Every mobile SDK sends it; a browser SDK omits it.

launch_source.description: Signals v3. What brought the user into the app. Precedence when several signals arrive: push, shortcut, widget, email, universal_link, deep_link, direct. A link whose query carries wsrc=widget or wsrc=shortcut is that source; a link carrying wmid is email. Required from SDKs that run signalsV3.

whisperr_message_id.description: Signals v3. At most 128 characters. Only for launch_source push (from the notification data) or email (the wmid link parameter).

link_route.description: Signals v3. At most 256 characters. The path of the link that won, never the query or fragment. A segment that is all digits, a UUID, or 16 characters or longer becomes :id. A custom-scheme link has no host: its route is / plus everything between scheme:// and the query.

link_host.description: Signals v3. The host of an http(s) link (universal link, Android app link, web landing URL). Never for a custom scheme.

utm_source.description: Signals v3. At most 128 characters. Copied from the link only when present.

utm_medium.description: Signals v3. At most 128 characters. Copied from the link only when present.

utm_campaign.description: Signals v3. At most 128 characters. Copied from the link only when present.

first_after_update.description: Signals v3, optional. true on the first app_opened after app_updated; omitted otherwise.

session_id.description: Signals v3. The same value as context.session_id.

screen_count.description: Signals v3. screen_viewed events in this foreground visit.

unique_screen_count.description: Signals v3. Distinct screen_name values in this foreground visit.

event_count.description: Signals v3. Customer track() events in this foreground visit. Automatic (reserved) events do not count.

error_count.description: Signals v3. app_error occurrences in this foreground visit, including the ones the per-session cap or the fingerprint dedupe dropped.

reserved.name: screen_viewed
reserved.trigger: The app calls the SDK screen API, or a framework navigation hook the SDK installs.

screen_name.description: The screen name the app or the navigation framework gives.

reserved.name: push_opened
reserved.trigger: The user opens a notification whose data carries whisperr_message_id.

deep_link.description: Copied from the notification data when present.

action_id.description: Contract v2. default for a tap on the notification body; otherwise the identifier of the action button the user tapped.

cold_start.description: Contract v2. true when the open launched the app process; false when the app was already running.

reserved.name: push_received
reserved.trigger: Contract v2. The device receives a push whose data carries whisperr_message_id. Once per message id on this device.

foreground.description: true when the app was in the foreground when the push arrived.

source.description: The code path that saw the push: the in-app foreground handler, the iOS Notification Service Extension, the Android messaging service, or an Expo background task.

reserved.name: push_permission_changed
reserved.trigger: The SDK first learns the notification permission, or learns that it changed since the last value it sent. Mobile SDKs read it on each move to the foreground where the platform makes this cheap; the app can also report it.

previous_status.description: The last status the SDK sent from this device. Omitted on the first report.

alerts_enabled.description: Signals v3, optional. The platform reports that alerts are shown. Sent only where the platform exposes it.

lock_screen.description: Signals v3, optional. The platform reports that notifications show on the lock screen. Sent only where the platform exposes it.

scheduled_summary.description: Signals v3, optional. iOS: notifications go to the scheduled summary. Sent only where the platform exposes it.

time_sensitive.description: Signals v3, optional. iOS: time-sensitive notifications are allowed. Sent only where the platform exposes it.

channel_blocked.description: Signals v3, optional. Android: the notification channel the SDK posts to is blocked. Sent only where the platform exposes it.

reserved.name: app_error
reserved.trigger: Signals v3. An uncaught error the SDK's global handlers see (unless captureErrors is false), or an app call to trackError(error, {screen?, kind?}). At most one per fingerprint per session and at most 20 per session. Never flushes on its own.

error_kind.description: js, dart or native for an uncaught error of that runtime; handled (the default) for trackError; network or screen when the app passes that kind.

fatal.description: true when the runtime is about to terminate.

error_name.description: At most 64 characters. The error class or type only (TypeError, HTTP_500). Never the message.

fingerprint.description: 16 lowercase hex characters: the start of the SHA-256 of error_name and the function names of the top three stack frames (paths, line and column numbers stripped), joined by a newline. Without a stack, the SHA-256 of error_name alone. See signalsV3.fingerprintVectors.

screen_name.description: The screen_name of the last screen_viewed (or the screen the app passes to trackError). Omitted when there is none.

reserved.name: app_crashed
reserved.trigger: Signals v3, mobile. The previous run of the app ended abnormally. Sent on the next launch, before that launch's app_opened. Never in a debug build.

crash_kind.description: abnormal_exit when only the unclean-shutdown flag shows it; crash when a fatal handler recorded the error.

crashed_app_version.description: The app version of the run that crashed.

crashed_session_id.description: The session_id of the run that crashed.

crashed_screen_name.description: The last screen_name of the run that crashed.

foreground.description: true when the app was in the foreground when it ended.

pushEventsV2.description: Contract v2 push events (SPEC.md -> Automatic events). Opt-in: an SDK that implements push_received and the v2 push_opened properties runs these cases on the same harness as `cases`, and skips the legacy cases listed in supersedes. Two v2 steps: `receivePush` hands the data payload to the SDK's receipt path named by `source`, with the app in the foreground or not (`foreground`); an SDK that has no such path skips the case. `openPush` hands the data payload to the SDK's push-open API; `actionId` is the tapped action button (absent: a tap on the notification body), and `launchedApp` says whether the open launched the process (the app reads it as the initial notification). When an expected event names `context`, the harness checks the governed context keys as v2.json does: a named key must be equal, an unnamed governed key (app_version, app_build, platform, sdk_name, sdk_version, locale) must be absent; without `context` it removes context as for `cases`.

signalsV3.description: Signals v3 (SPEC.md -> Engagement signals): context.session_id on every event, launch_source and link properties on app_opened, per-visit counters on app_backgrounded, app_error, app_crashed. Opt-in per section: an SDK runs a section when it implements that feature and its kind of SDK is in appliesTo. An SDK that runs any section sends launch_source and the app_backgrounded counters on every app_opened / app_backgrounded (the catalogue marks them requiredIn signalsV3) and implements pushEventsV2. Harness: the automatic.json harness with these changes. Steps: launch may carry via (launchSource) and, for web, url; track calls track(name) with no properties (the event is compared with properties {} and no common properties); trackError and uncaughtError (errors); config.captureErrors and config.debugBuild. Every expected event names context.session_id as a $session_<x> placeholder: the harness binds it to the first value it sees, every later use must carry the same value, distinct placeholders must carry distinct values, and every value must match sess_ plus a lowercase UUID v4. The harness checks no other context key here (v2.json versionContext pins those). Other placeholders: $fp_<x> binds like $session_<x>; $error_kind is the SDK's uncaught-error kind (js for React Native and web, dart for Flutter, native for Swift); $fatal_detected_by is js_fatal, dart_fatal or native_exception for the same SDKs. Attribution window: the harness flushes after every step, and that flush ends an open window (the SDK sends a held app_opened with what it knows, launch_source direct by default), so no case waits 1500 ms. Legacy cases: when an SDK that runs signalsV3 runs cases and pushEventsV2.cases, the harness drops the events named in legacyStrip.events and removes the legacyStrip.properties keys from every sent event before it compares, so those cases keep their v1 meaning.

sessionsAndCounters.description: Session id and per-visit counters. Every event carries context.session_id (sess_ plus a UUID v4). A cold start always starts a new session; otherwise the id changes only after 30 minutes with no event (lazy: the next event gets the new id). app_backgrounded carries the same id as session_id and the counters for the foreground visit that ends.

launchSource.description: launch_source on app_opened. launch.via hands the launch signal to the SDK while the attribution window is open: push goes to the push-open API as a body tap that launched the app; link goes to the SDK's launch-URL path (initial URL / open URL); shortcut goes to the SDK's quick-action path (an SDK without one skips that case). The SDK sends the held app_opened as soon as the source resolves, before the event that resolved it (push_opened), and only the winning signal supplies whisperr_message_id, link_route, link_host and utm_*.

errors.description: app_error. trackError builds an error whose type name is name and calls the SDK's trackError(error, {kind, screen}). uncaughtError raises an error of that type through the runtime's global handler (RN ErrorUtils, Flutter FlutterError.onError, Swift the uncaught-exception handler); before it builds the client, the harness installs its own handler and checks that the SDK still calls it for every uncaught error. The harness cannot control the stack, so fingerprints are $fp_<x> placeholders (bound like $session_<x>; each must be 16 lowercase hex characters); the SDK checks its fingerprint function against fingerprintVectors.

crashes.description: app_crashed from the unclean-shutdown flag. On each foreground the SDK persists {running, session_id, screen, app_version}; on background it clears it; a fatal handler records last_fatal. At launch a set flag sends app_crashed before that launch's app_opened (after app_installed / app_updated). config.debugBuild true makes the SDK's debug-build check (__DEV__, kDebugMode, #if DEBUG) report a debug build; every other case reports a release build.

firstAfterUpdate.description: Optional. first_after_update: true on the first app_opened after app_updated, and on no other app_opened.

web.description: Browser SDKs. launch loads url (the landing URL in location) and makes the page visible; background is visibilitychange to hidden; foreground is visibilitychange to visible. One app_opened per web session (each new session_id), without cold_start. launch_source: wmid on the landing URL is email (whisperr_message_id = wmid), else wsrc widget or shortcut, else direct. link_route and link_host come from location, utm_* when present. foreground_ms counts the visible period that ends. The web harness has no app version, and it compares only app_opened, app_backgrounded and app_error; it drops every other event before comparing.
